summary: Completed the bounded independent source review of isolated M3 run/stream/auth changes against the inherited M2 overlay. Found two medium issues: fixed-window scheduler starvation, and an inherited NOTIFY-send loss path left uncovered by M3 resync handling. No additional supported findings in scoped run fencing, shutdown, current SSE authorization or OIDC admission checks. This is not the final M3 runtime gate.
coverage: Reviewed isolated source only as the implementation subject: /Users/artem/visua/.check/evidence-automation-20261013, base b34cf1fe846920c98aa71df3121712284880dc1a with inherited M2 hashes in automation-worktree-baseline.json. Initial and final SHA256 values are recorded in automation-boundary-review-source.json. VisuaService changed concurrently in proposal approval validation; after detecting its changed file hash, I re-read run recording, connector fencing, scheduler, shutdown, host/proposal fencing and repeated the scheduler reproduction against the final recorded bytes. Other tracked files remained unchanged.

Traced services/visua.ts RunRecorder, start/claim/reconcile/heartbeat/cancel/interrupt/save/stop, connector result/error writes, host proposals and step persistence; run-execution.ts ownership matching; storage/store.ts scans, workspace locking, transactions and afterCommit; SQLite serialization and PostgreSQL advisory transaction locks. Checked stage/run type compatibility and server startup/shutdown ordering, including index.ts process exit handling.

Traced workspace-events.ts ready/event/ping checks, current-authorization promise lifetime, idle checks, storage timeout, queue count/bytes, event compaction, resync and abort/shutdown cleanup; app.ts canonical workspace and captured credential wiring; auth/service.ts current session/token/user/member/tenant/workspace/SSO role checks and no-touch session semantics.

Traced tenant SSO generation updates, per-instance discovery cache validation, persisted login generation, post-token-exchange provider/admission reload and session grant transaction in auth/service.ts, with identity store flow/session/connection support. External token exchange remains outside the callback grant transaction.

Traced bus.ts, storage/events.ts LISTEN reconnect and NOTIFY send behavior, and web/lib/events.ts full-query refresh/transient-activity reset after open, resync or compacted events. Inspected query refresh defaults and agent activity ownership. Compared root M2 storage/events.ts reference only after verifying its SHA256 equals the pinned M2 manifest; the failed-send handler is unchanged.

Read run-reliability.test.ts, workspace-events.test.ts, stream-auth.test.ts, oidc-current.test.ts, relay.test.ts, relevant startup.test.ts shutdown cases and web/test/events.test.ts as coverage evidence, including pending PostgreSQL-specific cases; none of those suites were executed in this review.

Executed two small synthetic reproductions using the isolated source with VISUA_DATABASE_URL and VISUA_TEST_DATABASE_URL unset: actual in-memory SQLite RunCollection/reconcileRuns with launches observed but no agents invoked; and actual PgEventRelay/EventBus with fake pg clients/execute transport and no network. Scripts and recorded outcomes are under automation-review-reproductions/.

findings.mechanism: A fixed oldest-256 active scan can be filled entirely by queued runs whose workspace slots are occupied. Reconciliation retries that same window without advancing a cursor; rejected claims do not move queued rows. Later eligible workspace runs and later expired/legacy running rows are never examined while those older queues remain blocked. This also lets abandoned running rows remain unreconciled indefinitely when continuously heartbeated live work keeps the earlier queues blocked.
findings.evidence: Observed with actual isolated source and in-memory SQLite in automation-review-reproductions/scheduler-starvation.mjs: eight workspaces each have 32 older queued records and a valid running lease, followed by an eligible run in a free workspace and a legacy abandoned running record. There are 266 active rows, but active() returns 256. Three successive actual reconcileRuns() calls launch nothing; eligible-late stays queued and expired-late stays running. The script replaces only launch with an observation callback to avoid agent execution; neither omitted run reaches it. Continued starvation while blockers remain is inferred from the unchanged scan predicate/order and observed repeated results.
findings.recommendation: Keep each tick bounded while advancing fairly through active work, such as a stable rotating/keyset scan or eligible-workspace selection. Ensure expired-run reconciliation cannot be hidden behind queued rows. Add a regression with more than 256 active records and assert that a later free workspace progresses and a later abandoned lease is fenced.

findings.mechanism: A committed mutation whose publisher-side pg_notify operation fails is only logged and dropped. If the dedicated LISTEN connections and browser SSE connections stay healthy, no reconnect occurs and M3 emits no resync. A remote browser therefore misses the change and can keep stale canonical data until another relevant invalidation or reconnect. This handler is inherited from M2, but it remains an omission in the scoped M3 lost-relay-event recovery contract; it is not claimed as a newly introduced regression.
findings.evidence: Observed with actual isolated PgEventRelay/EventBus and a fake transport in automation-review-reproductions/relay-send-gap.mjs: one simulated NOTIFY failure followed by a successful unrelated event, with both listeners continuously connected. Result: sends=2, failedSends=1, listenerConnections=2, received=[later-unrelated-event], resyncs=0. Source inspection shows only LISTEN recovery calls bus.resync; the send catch only logs. The root M2 reference hash 0538bf546b8a072cc88fef0d3f947efd27892195a2053746b18c9d8fc93bddbc matches the baseline manifest and its failed-send handler is identical. Remote UI staleness is inferred from the browser invalidation mapping; this was not a live PostgreSQL/browser test.
findings.recommendation: Cover publisher-side gaps with bounded retryable resync delivery to affected remote subscribers after send recovery, or durable revision/gap detection that causes canonical refetch. A local-only bus.resync would not repair other instances. Add a failed-send regression that keeps listeners connected and verifies the remote stream receives an explicit resync before cached state is trusted.

limitations: No live PostgreSQL, database/container, server/browser, provider/connector/network, full suites, build, git, deployment or delegation was used. The required two-instance PostgreSQL acceptance gate remains unverified by this report; source test coverage is not an executed pass.

The scheduler reproduction uses actual in-memory SQLite storage and scheduler code with synthetic persisted running leases and an observation-only launch override. It demonstrates scan selection/starvation, not cross-process PostgreSQL locking behavior.

The relay reproduction replaces pg clients and the notification transport, so it establishes application handling of a failed send but does not measure live PostgreSQL connection failure rates or browser cache behavior.

The M2 manifest pins baseline files by hash. Exact historical bytes were compared only for storage/events.ts using the explicitly authorized root reference after its digest matched; the implementation subject throughout is the isolated M3 checkout.

Review is limited to the assigned durable-run/current-authorization/stream boundary. Strict proposal payload validation, citation authority, policy/check claims, general rate limits and broader M3 UI/acceptance work are outside this review.

Concurrent lead edits to VisuaService proposal approval validation occurred during the pass. The final scoped run/connector/proposal fencing source was re-read and the scheduler reproduction was repeated; broader proposal semantics remain outside this review. Any later source change requires affected-scope revalidation.
